title: [Bug]: NC31 logs "Capabilities of OCA\\CloudFederationAPI\\Capabilities took 0.xx seconds to generate" on every page refresh.
body:
### ⚠️ This issue respects the following points: ⚠️

- [x] This is a **bug**, not a question or a configuration/webserver/proxy issue.
- [x] This issue is **not** already reported on [Github](https://github.com/nextcloud/server/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue+label%3Abug) OR [Nextcloud Community Forum](https://<redacted-host>/) _(I've searched it)_.
- [x] Nextcloud Server **is** up to date. See [Maintenance and Release Schedule](https://github.com/nextcloud/server/wiki/Maintenance-and-Release-Schedule) for supported versions.
- [x] I agree to follow Nextcloud's [Code of Conduct](https://nextcloud.com/contribute/code-of-conduct/).

### Bug description

Installed NC31, the logs are getting flooded with this on every page refresh:
```
{"reqId":"j8pdPAqNLGYF8f4854Dh","level":3,"time":"2025-03-21T08:24:01+01:00","remoteAddr":":<nick>:93.237.197.xx","user":"admin","app":"no app in context","method":"GET","url":"/apps/dashboard/","message":"Capabilities of OCA\\CloudFederationAPI\\Capabilities took 1.09 seconds to generate.","userAgent":"Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64; rv:136.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/136.0","version":"31.0.2.1","data":[]}
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install NC31
2. Choose to install the recommended apps when asked after login
3. Look at the log


### Expected behavior

No message in the log.

### Nextcloud Server version

31

### Operating system

Debian/Ubuntu

### PHP engine version

PHP 8.3

### Web server

Nginx

### Database engine version

MariaDB

### Is this bug present after an update or on a fresh install?

Fresh Nextcloud Server install

### Are you using the Nextcloud Server Encryption module?

Encryption is Disabled

### What user-backends are you using?

- [x] Default user-backend _(database)_
- [ ] LDAP/ Active Directory
- [ ] SSO - SAML
- [ ] Other

comments.author: participant12
comments.body:
The key pairs are managed by [IdentityProofManager](https://github.com/nextcloud/server/blob/520d8beaf54842795fa1277b1831635545d2b035/lib/private/Security/IdentityProof/Manager.php#L103) which store the data in 2 files (public/private) within appdata. On s3 it mights be enough to trigger the warning.

I am curious on the original request that still pops those warning in logs since 31.0.4, but https://github.com/nextcloud/server/pull/51946 should have been enough. Are they still generated when reaching `/login` like it was previously stated in the original message of this thread.

Now, the key pair should only be necessary when requesting the `/ocm-provider/` endpoint, and not as a global capabilities. 
I will move things around.

However, there is some needed task in here:

- do not use a global `IOCMProvider` in `OCMDiscoveryService`
- manage the generation of the `IOCMProvider` for the local instance outside of `OCA\CloudFederationAPI\Capabilities`
- rewrite the code logic behind `ResourceTypeRegisterEvent`
- ~~deprecate the `ResourceTypeRegisterEvent` and replace with 2 events: one for capabilities (light process), one for the /ocm/ endpoint (heavier process)~~
